source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ እቤ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ሠናይ፡ ዕፀ፡ ወ†*ሠናይ፡ ለርእይ፡† ወአዳም፡ ቈጽሉ፡ ወ†ፍሬሁኒ፡† ሞገስ፡ ጥቀ፡ ለርእዩ፡ ገጽ።

translation.text: Then I said, “This is a beautiful tree, beautiful to look at[a]; its leaves are lovely, and its fruit[b] is very pleasing to look at.”

footnotes.text: The printed Ethiopic appearance expression is dagger-marked as difficult. In p.62 note9 Charles prefers a Greek fragrance reading; this candidate retains his printed Ethiopic appearance sense.
The printed Ethiopic has fruit, marked with daggers. Charles p.62 note10 proposes flowers with a Greek comparison; fruit here follows the printed main text.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ፩እምነ፡ መላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ወክቡራን፡ እንዘ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘዲቤሆሙ።

translation.text: Then Michael, one of the holy and honored angels who was with me, answered me—he who was over them.[a]

footnotes.text: Michael is the subject. The closing expression says he was over them without naming the plural referent here; honored may also be rendered glorious. The following chapter supplies his speech, which is not imported.
